answers.answer: Shuffle the Factory deck, randomly select players + 1 cards face-down on the board, and return the rest to the box without looking. Put one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories. Randomly choose one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts, then play proceeds clockwise.
answers.evidence: Setup: Factory cards, encounter tokens, structure bonus; lowest-numbered Player Mat starts

answers.answer: Each player's character starts at their home base; two workers start on the two land-adjoined territories adjoining it; four mechs start over the abilities on the Faction Mat; six stars are by the faction emblem; six technology cubes are in the Player Mat green boxes marked with a black square; four structures are in their matching Player Mat boxes; four recruits are on its bottom-row circular spaces; six remaining workers are on its Produce red rectangles; and the action token is beside the Player Mat ready for its first placement. The Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw. The Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins, and two objective cards.
answers.evidence: Setup: starting positions table and starting power/combat-card draw versus popularity/coins/objectives

answers.answer: You must move the token to a different section from last turn, but may then take neither action, the top action only, the bottom action only, or both. The bottom action cannot come first when taking both. Rusviet may repeat a section, but each top and bottom action can still be taken only once that turn. Top-row gains may pay the bottom-row cost. Pay every exposed red-box cost in full before taking benefits; benefits are the exposed green boxes, and you may take as much or as little as desired. Bottom costs and coin benefits depend on the Player Mat and upgrades.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: different section, optional top then bottom, red costs and green benefits

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls that territory and all its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities; you retain those abilities even without control, except an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. You may pay an action's resource cost using resources from any territories you currently control, even when taking the action elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: enemy worker control; opponents do not gain buildings' abilities; costs use resources from any controlled territory

answers.answer: On a normal unupgraded Move, you may select up to two different units and move each one adjacent territory; you cannot select one unit twice. All units can pick up, carry, and drop any number of resources. Only mechs may also carry any number of your workers, never your character. A carried worker may later move itself, or it may move onto a mech and be carried by that mech's subsequent move.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: two different units; all units carry resources; mechs carry workers; carried workers may subsequently move

answers.answer: A Speed-enabled mech entering a territory with enemy workers only stops and cannot move again that turn. The enemy workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources; you lose one popularity per worker, down to zero, and having zero or insufficient popularity does not prevent the retreat. This is not combat. Your workers cannot independently enter the territory while enemy workers control it.
answers.evidence: Move: enemy workers only; Speed stops are overridden by enemy-unit stops

answers.answer: After all units finish moving in the Move action, resolve combats before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order when there are multiple combats. Your workers cannot independently move into or out of a territory controlled by enemy characters or mechs. Your character or mech may enter, but stops and cannot move again that turn.
answers.evidence: Move: enemy character/mechs; finish moving other units, then resolve all combats before the bottom-row action

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card before upgrades; if the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck, and if both deck and discard are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources, same or different, or one popularity, before upgrades. Put traded resources on a controlled territory containing at least one worker; if all your workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources. Built Monument adds one popularity to Bolster, and built Armory adds one power to Trade.
answers.evidence: Bolster and Trade action descriptions

answers.answer: For Produce, first pay every exposed Produce cost in full, including any power, popularity, and/or coins. Then, before upgrades, choose up to two different controlled territories; each worker in those territories may produce one matching terrain token on that same territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and go in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Newly exposed costs affect future Produce actions and do not change the cost already paid. A controlled Mill adds one bonus production territory; the Mill counts as one producing worker and actual workers there may also produce normally.
answers.evidence: Produce: numbered resolution steps and Mill rules

answers.answer: Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens shown in exposed Upgrade cost boxes on your Player Mat; Deploy costs the number of metal tokens shown in exposed Deploy cost boxes. Each amount varies by mat and upgrades. For Upgrade, move a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box to improve a top benefit and reduce a bottom cost; solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded. For Deploy, choose a mech on your Faction Mat and place it on a controlled territory containing your worker, never a lake; its uncovered ability then applies to your character and every mech, not workers. Even after completing all upgrades, mechs, structures, and recruits, you may still pay for the corresponding bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: Upgrade, Deploy, and completed bottom actions

answers.answer: Build a structure on a controlled territory containing your worker; the Factory is allowed, but lakes and home bases are forbidden, and only one structure total may be on a territory. Structures cannot be moved or destroyed. An enemy unit on the Mill's territory means you do not control it, so it cannot produce there; the Mill's bonus applies only while controlled. Your Mine remains your personal tunnel for your units even when an enemy controls its territory, so you may move to and from it subject to ordinary entry and combat restrictions. Opponents cannot use your buildings' abilities.
answers.evidence: Build: placement restrictions and structure abilities; Mine personal tunnel; Mill only while controlled

answers.answer: When enlisting, take a recruit from any bottom-row section of your Player Mat and put it permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus on your Faction Mat. Immediately gain the chosen one-time bonus: two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is the circle uncovered where the recruit was removed from, independent of the one-time bonus chosen. When bonuses trigger, resolve the active player first, then the left neighbor, then the right neighbor, checking for a sixth star and stopping if it ends the game. In a two-player game, the opponent triggers the bonus once, not twice.
answers.evidence: Enlist and Ongoing recruits: one-time bonuses, uncovered circle, resolution order, and two-player rule

answers.answer: Both combatants simultaneously and secretly choose dial power from zero up to the lesser of seven or their current power, and may add up to one combat card per participating character or mech, even with zero dial power. Rusviet People's Army adds one additional card total if any workers are present. If both combatants have combat mech abilities, the attacker uses theirs first, then the defender. Reveal simultaneously and add dial power and card values; the attacker wins ties. Each player deducts their selected dial power from the Power Track, and every played combat card is discarded face-up; card values do not cost extra track power.
answers.evidence: Combat: steps 1–4

answers.answer: The winner controls the territory and its resources. All losing characters, mechs, and workers retreat to their owner's home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy allows eligible units and carried workers to retreat to adjacent lakes instead. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none, and Polania Camaraderie removes that popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after Polania wins as aggressor on its turn; it does not protect against driving off undefended workers without combat. A non-Saxony winner with zero or one combat stars places one, and one with two places none; Saxony places one after every victory while it has star tokens. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
answers.evidence: Combat: steps 5–6

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if your character remains in the token territory; discard the token and draw a card before a following bottom action. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token stays. Gains of resources, workers, mechs, and structures go to the encounter territory. Pay the encounter's printed cost, but no additional normal action cost applies and no additional Player Mat benefits or ongoing recruit bonuses are gained.
answers.evidence: Encounters: timing after Move and combats; contested entry; destination; costs and bonuses

answers.answer: Every player's character, on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if needed), must look at the available Factory cards, choose one, and return the rest. This applies to each player, not just the first visitor; each player gets at most one permanent card, and later visits cannot exchange it. The card is a fifth action section with optional top then bottom, subject to the usual no-repeat rule and Rusviet's exception; similar Factory actions give no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. The Factory bottom action moves one unit up to two territories within that Move action, or up to three for a character or mech with Speed, subject to Mine access and normal movement/stop restrictions.
answers.evidence: Factory: card selection and Factory action rules

answers.answer: Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective; you may wait, but must meet all its requirements at the moment of reveal. Place a star on the objective space of the Triumph Track and return the completed card to the bottom of the objective deck; normally return your other objective card there too. Normally a player may earn only one objective star. Saxony may complete both starting objectives for up to two objective stars and keeps its other card after completing the first.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements: reveal timing, requirements, resolution, and Saxony exception

answers.answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, combat victories (up to two combat stars, with Saxony's exception), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony's exception. A placed star is permanent even if power or popularity later drops, and another player's stars never block a goal. The game ends immediately when someone places their sixth star, with no equalizing turns or further actions.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: Stars and immediate end

answers.answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, collect its primary benefit, coins, and the active player's ongoing recruit benefit before placing that star. For a neighbor's power/popularity recruit star, finish the active action, then resolve active player first, left neighbor, and right neighbor, checking for the sixth star at each step; if one has already ended the game, no later recruit star or bonus resolves. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle when the game ends, undo that part of movement by returning initiating units to the territories they came from; do not resolve another combat.
answers.evidence: Sixth star sequence and unresolved battle rule

answers.answer: At 10 popularity, the 7–12 rate applies: five stars add 5 × $4 = $20; four normal territories plus the Factory count as four + three = seven territories, adding 7 × $3 = $21; and 13 controlled resources make six complete pairs, adding 6 × $2 = $12. Together these add $53 to held coins, before any structure bonus. The selected structure bonus is scored from your structures even if opponents control their territories. Tiebreakers are, in order: workers + mechs + structures (not character), power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, then stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune: popularity rates, Factory territory count, complete resource pairs, structure bonus eligibility, and tie order

answers.answer: A home base is not a territory for any game effect. By default you cannot move back into any home base, build there, or deploy there; setup, forced retreats, and Crimea's unlocked Wayfare are exceptions. Two expansion-placeholder home bases without matching core factions are inactive.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: home base definition and exceptions; inactive expansion placeholders

answers.answer: Mountain produces metal; tundra produces oil; farm produces food; forest produces wood; village produces a worker. Lakes and the Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.
answers.evidence: Produce terrain/product table; Control, resources and home bases: resource types and supply limit

answers.answer: Any unit may pick up, carry, and drop any number of resources during movement; a mech may also carry any number of your workers, but cannot carry your character. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character or mech, not workers. A tunnel jump costs one movement step, and the extra step may be before or after it; a mech may pick up or drop resources and workers mid-movement. Stops for enemy units and character encounters override Speed.
answers.evidence: Move: carrying and Speed rules

answers.answer: Yes. Any unit may enter a territory containing only an enemy structure and take control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.
answers.evidence: Move: Enemy structure only; printed tunnel territories

answers.answer: You may not pay only part of a cost. If you cannot afford any action, take a dead turn: move your token to a different section and take neither action.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: dead turn and never pay only part of a cost

answers.answer: A built Armory grants one power when you take Trade, and a built Monument grants one popularity when you take Bolster. These are bonuses to those matching top actions. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities, and you retain those abilities even without control; the exception is that an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce.
answers.evidence: Bolster and Trade; Control, resources and home bases: structure abilities

answers.answer: Riverwalk is an unlockable mech ability for every faction, including Nordic; it lets your character and all your mechs cross rivers, not workers. Nordic and Saxony Riverwalk to forests and mountains; Rusviet to farms and villages; Crimea to farms and tundra; Polania to villages and mountains. Nordic Swim is separate: it lets workers alone cross rivers to any land terrain, not lakes; it does not grant lake movement to workers or confer Swim on Nordic mechs.
answers.evidence: Riverwalk destinations and Nordic Swim description

answers.answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels, including your Mine, adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. These shortcuts are for characters and mechs, not workers.
answers.evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities: Underpass and Township

answers.answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or your Mine: the opponent loses two power on the track, once per combat, not once per unit. Nordic Artillery applies before combat and may be used by paying one power to reduce the opponent's power by two; it too is once per combat, not per unit.
answers.evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities: Disarm and Artillery

answers.answer: With at least one worker present, Rusviet People's Army permits one additional combat card total. Two mechs normally allow two cards, so with three workers present they may play three cards total. Workers alone never fight; a character or mech is still required.
answers.evidence: Rusviet Township/People's Army; Combat steps 2

answers.answer: With Wayfare, Crimea's character and mechs may move from a territory or home base to your own home base or any inactive faction home base, regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. They cannot move to an active opponent's home base.
answers.evidence: Crimea Wayfare description

answers.answer: Crimea Scout steals one random combat card from an opponent into your hand before combat, once per combat, not per unit. Crimea Coercion lets you spend one combat card once per turn as any one resource, regardless of the card's value.
answers.evidence: Crimea Scout and Coercion descriptions

answers.answer: Nordic Seaworthy lets characters and mechs move to and from lakes, and lets them retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home; mechs may carry workers with them. Polania Submerge lets characters and mechs move to and from lakes and move from any lake to any other lake, but Polania has no adjacent-lake retreat exception. With either lake ability, workers on lakes require a mech to move off, and you cannot leave carried workers or resources behind on a lake when their carrier leaves.
answers.evidence: Nordic Seaworthy; Polania Submerge; lake-carrier restrictions

answers.answer: Polania Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after Polania wins combat as the aggressor on its turn. It does not prevent popularity loss for driving off undefended workers without combat.
answers.evidence: Polania Camaraderie description

answers.answer: Polania may choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order; it is one drawn card, not two. Pay each option's printed cost, and the gain from the first option may pay the second option's cost. Polania may choose fewer than two options; unlike factions without Meander, it is not required to choose one affordable option, and unaffordable coin/popularity options cannot be selected.
answers.evidence: Polania Meander; Encounters: option choice and affordability

answers.answer: During Factory bottom Move, a character that enters an encounter-token territory stops and cannot move again that turn. The encounter resolves only after the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there; it does not occur before the combats finish.
answers.evidence: Encounters: applies during Factory Move; after whole Move action and all combats

answers.answer: Coins are not hidden information, but you need not reveal their total value when asked. Combat-card hand count is public, though during combat you may conceal whether you committed any cards until reveal; card contents are secret until revealed. Objective contents are secret until you reveal a completed objective.
answers.evidence: Public and hidden information table

answers.answer: Players may make informal agreements, but they are unenforceable. Coins are the only tangible items exchangeable; tournament play forbids even coin exchanges for deals or alliances. Negotiation cannot cancel combat once movement of plastic units onto opposing units has initiated it; fight after Move, though bribes may influence the outcome.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements

answers.answer: At popularity 0–6, each star scores $3, each territory count scores $2, and each complete pair of controlled resources scores $1. At 7–12, the rates are $4 per star, $3 per territory count, and $2 per resource pair. At 13–18, the rates are $5, $4, and $3, respectively. Controlled lakes count as territories; home bases do not. Pool controlled resources across your territories and ignore an odd leftover token.
answers.evidence: Final fortune: controlled territories/resources and popularity rate table

answers.answer: For tunnels adjacent to structures, count each unique printed tunnel territory once across all structures; Mines do not count, and payouts are 1: $2, 2–3: $4, 4–5: $6, 6: $9. For lakes adjacent to structures, count unique lakes once; payouts are 1: $2, 2–3: $4, 4–5: $6, 6–7: $9. For encounters adjacent to structures, count unique printed encounter locations once even if the token was removed; payouts are 1: $2, 2–3: $4, 4–5: $6, 6–7: $9. Rivers do not break adjacency.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus eligibility: adjacency tiles and adjacency counting rule

answers.answer: For structures on tunnels, count structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines; payouts are 1: $2, 2: $4, 3–4: $6. For structures in a row, count only your longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break the line, and payouts are 1: $2, 2: $4, 3: $6, 4: $9. For structures on farms/tundras, combine qualifying structures on both terrain types; payouts are 1: $2, 2: $4, 3: $6, 4: $9.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus eligibility: structures on tunnels, in a row, and on farms/tundras

answers.answer: Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.
answers.evidence: Combat step 6: attacker loses popularity even for workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake

answers.answer: A popularity star is permanent once placed, even if your popularity later drops; it does not protect your current popularity or the scoring tier, which uses current popularity at game end. Other players' stars never block a goal, so two factions may each place a star for achieving the same type of goal.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end: placed stars permanent; other players' stars never block a goal; current popularity scores

answers.answer: Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat near your faction's home base, following clockwise from the top of the board: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, omitting inactive factions. The relative order determines who is immediately left and right, and those neighbors can receive ongoing recruit bonuses when the active player takes the corresponding bottom-row action.
answers.evidence: Setup: random mat deal and clockwise seating order; Ongoing recruits: immediate left and right neighbors

answers.answer: A river is a border between two land territories. A lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. A unit with an applicable lake-movement ability may enter the lake from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
answers.evidence: Move: river and lake definitions; lake entry from surrounding land territories

answers.answer: No. When an encounter card is drawn, show it to all players, show its artwork, and read its capitalized thematic text aloud. You do not have to read every option aloud.
answers.evidence: Encounters: show card and artwork, read capitalized thematic text; options need not be read aloud

answers.answer: There is no limit on the number of your friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: no limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory

answers.answer: The next clockwise player may begin their turn after the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, while the current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure, or recruit to gain.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: next player may begin after noninteractive bottom-row action starts

answers.answer: No. Each chosen top action and bottom action is limited to once within the turn. Rusviet may repeat a section, but that does not allow repeating either action within the turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: chosen top and bottom actions each limited to once, including Rusviet

answers.answer: The normal unupgraded Move action lets you gain $1 instead of moving units.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: move up to two different units or alternatively gain $1

answers.answer: No. Workers never return to the Player Mat. A worker that retreats goes to its home base (or, where the Nordic Seaworthy retreat exception applies, an adjacent lake), not back to the Player Mat; workers cannot be returned to cover or pay a Produce cost.
answers.evidence: Produce: workers never return to the Player Mat; Move and Combat retreat destinations

answers.answer: Yes. You may attack with zero power, zero popularity, or both.
answers.evidence: Combat: you may attack with zero power/popularity

answers.answer: Yes. A non-Saxony player may still fight after reaching the limit of two combat stars; additional victories simply do not award another combat star.
answers.evidence: Combat: may still fight after reaching combat-star limit

answers.answer: A faction without Meander must choose one affordable encounter option and cannot decline to choose any option. It cannot select an unaffordable coin or popularity option and must pay the printed cost, but it may take as little of the chosen option's benefit as desired.
answers.evidence: Encounters: required affordable choice, unaffordable options, costs, and optional benefits

answers.answer: Combatants do not choose in turn order: both simultaneously and secretly choose their dial power and optional combat cards. They reveal simultaneously; card contents remain secret until reveal.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–3: simultaneous secret choice and simultaneous reveal; card contents secret until revealed

answers.answer: Announce the bottom-row action to the other players so your neighbors can check and resolve their applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: announce the action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses

answers.answer: Place a star as soon as its goal is achieved; you cannot decline or delay it, and the sixth star immediately ends play. A completed objective differs because you may wait to reveal it, but may reveal only on your own turn before or after completing a top or bottom action and must still meet all requirements at that moment.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end; Objectives: reveal timing and may wait

answers.answer: No. Before applicable faction or mech abilities, units cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes; this restriction applies to characters, mechs, and workers.
answers.evidence: Move: units cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes; faction/mech exceptions

answers.answer: No. The recruit is placed permanently on the selected open one-time bonus space on your Faction Mat and cannot later move.
answers.evidence: Enlist: place recruit permanently; it cannot later move

answers.answer: No. Only a character triggers an encounter; a mech or worker entering the token territory does not resolve it or remove the token. A character stops when entering and the encounter resolves after the whole Move action and all combats only if the character remains there; then the token is discarded.
answers.evidence: Encounters: only character triggers; timing after Move and all combats

answers.answer: A controlled Mill provides one bonus production territory in addition to the normal allowance: two selected territories can become up to three, or an upgraded allowance of three can become up to four. The Mill counts as one producing worker, and actual workers on its territory also produce normally. The Mill can produce its terrain's matching token even when no actual worker is there.
answers.evidence: Produce: controlled Mill bonus allowance and output with or without actual worker

answers.answer: You control a territory if you have a unit there, or if you have a structure there and no enemy unit is present. Resources alone do not establish or preserve control; if your last unit leaves a territory with no structure, you no longer control it.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: unit or uncontested structure establishes control; resources are distinct

answers.answer: Build is paid with wood; Enlist is paid with food.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: Build—wood; Enlist—food
